Training Topic / Competency Item: Medical Error Prevention: includes study of root-cause analysis, error reduction and prevention, and patient safety
Purpose: Renewal - Mandatory Topic

Training Topic / Competency Item: Nursing Laws and Rules: current text of Florida Statutes Chapter 464 (Nurse Practice Act), Chapter 456 (Health Professions), and Chapter 64B9 of the Florida Administrative Code
Purpose: Renewal - Mandatory Topic
Notes / Research Flags: Hard mandate. Course must cover the current statutory and administrative code text governing nursing practice in Florida. Included within the 24-hr total.

Training Topic / Competency Item: Human Trafficking: identification of victims, reporting obligations, and available resources
Purpose: Renewal - Mandatory Topic
Notes / Research Flags: Hard mandate. Applies to RNs, LPNs, and APRNs every renewal cycle. Included within the 24-hr total.

Training Topic / Competency Item: Recognizing Impairment in the Workplace
Purpose: Renewal - Mandatory Topic
Notes / Research Flags: Alternating-cycle mandate. Applies every other biennial renewal. Included within the 24-hr total when applicable.

Training Topic / Competency Item: Domestic Violence: identification, intervention, and best practices for managing domestic violence situations
Purpose: Renewal - Mandatory Topic
Notes / Research Flags: Lower-frequency mandate. Adds 2h  above the base 24-hr requirement in the applicable cycle, bringing total to 26h  that renewal period.

Training Topic / Competency Item: HIV/AIDS: current Florida laws on AIDS and its impact on testing; confidentiality of test results; treatment of patients; protocols and procedures applicable to HIV counseling and testing, reporting, offering of HIV testing to pregnant women, and partner notification

Training Topic / Competency Item: General elective continuing education: any course relevant to the practice of nursing, provided by a Florida Board of Nursing-approved or ANCC-accredited provider

Training Topic / Competency Item: Nurse Assistant Certification Training Program (NATP): minimum 160 hours total - 60 hours classroom theory + 100 hours supervised clinical training
Purpose: Initial Certification
Approval Basis: CDPH-approved program; state competency exam required
Frequency: One-time (must complete within 4 months of employment)
Notes / Research Flags: State requirement exceeds federal 75-hr minimum. Must be completed at CDPH-approved NATP. No more than 15 students per instructor during clinical. Clinical hours 6am–8pm only. Competency exam required (NNAAP).

Training Topic / Competency Item: Pre-Contact Training (16 hours required before any direct resident contact): communications and interpersonal skills; infection control; safety and emergency procedures including Heimlich maneuver; promoting residents' independence; respecting residents' rights
Purpose: Initial Certification - Pre-Contact
Approval Basis: CDPH-approved program
Notes / Research Flags: These 5 topic areas are both state (22 CCR §71835) and federal (42 CFR §483.152(b)(1)) requirements. Must be completed before student may have any contact with a resident.

Training Topic / Competency Item: Module 1 - Introduction (2 hrs theory): role and responsibilities of the CNA; Title 22 Division 5 CCR overview; requirements for nurse assistant certification; professionalism; ethics and confidentiality
Purpose: Initial Certification
Approval Basis: CDPH-approved program

Training Topic / Competency Item: Module 2 - Patients' Rights (2 hrs theory / 1 hr clinical): resident rights as specified in 22 CCR §72527 and HSC §§1599.1, 1599.2, 1599.3 and 42 CFR §§483.10, 483.12, 483.13, 483.15
Purpose: Initial Certification
Approval Basis: CDPH-approved program

Training Topic / Competency Item: Module 3 - Body Mechanics (2 hrs theory / 3 hrs clinical): proper body mechanics; use of assistive devices; safe patient handling and transfer techniques
Purpose: Initial Certification
Approval Basis: CDPH-approved program

Training Topic / Competency Item: Module 4 - Infection Control (2 hrs theory / 3 hrs clinical): standard precautions; universal precautions; methods to handle patients and materials soiled with blood/body fluids; reducing transmission of infectious agents
Purpose: Initial Certification
Approval Basis: CDPH-approved program

Training Topic / Competency Item: Module 5 - Safety and Emergency Care (3 hrs theory / 3 hrs clinical): fall prevention; fire safety; emergency procedures; Heimlich maneuver; CPR awareness
Purpose: Initial Certification
Approval Basis: CDPH-approved program

Training Topic / Competency Item: Module 6 - Personal Care (6 hrs theory / 20 hrs clinical): bathing; oral hygiene; grooming; dressing; skin care; toileting; perineal care; continence care
Purpose: Initial Certification
Approval Basis: CDPH-approved program

Training Topic / Competency Item: Module 7 - Nutrition and Fluid Balance (4 hrs theory / 10 hrs clinical): assisting with meals; feeding techniques; nutritional needs; fluid intake and output measurement; dysphagia awareness
Purpose: Initial Certification
Approval Basis: CDPH-approved program

Training Topic / Competency Item: Module 8 - Musculoskeletal and Integumentary Care (4 hrs theory / 10 hrs clinical): skin observation; pressure ulcer prevention; range of motion; positioning; turning and repositioning
Purpose: Initial Certification
Approval Basis: CDPH-approved program

Training Topic / Competency Item: Module 9 - Elimination (3 hrs theory / 10 hrs clinical): bowel and bladder care; catheter care; ostomy care; documenting elimination
Purpose: Initial Certification
Approval Basis: CDPH-approved program

Training Topic / Competency Item: Module 10 - Vital Signs (3 hrs theory / 6 hrs clinical): taking and recording temperature, pulse, respirations, blood pressure; recognizing abnormal values and reporting to supervisor
Purpose: Initial Certification
Approval Basis: CDPH-approved program

Training Topic / Competency Item: Module 11 - Mental Health and Social Service Needs (2 hrs theory / 3 hrs clinical): behavior modification; aging process; responding to resident behavior; supporting resident dignity and autonomy; family involvement
Purpose: Initial Certification
Approval Basis: CDPH-approved program

Training Topic / Competency Item: Module 12 - Cognitive Impairment (4 hrs theory / 4 hrs clinical, including at least 4 hrs clinical for developmental/mental disorders): dementia and Alzheimer's care; communication with cognitively impaired residents; appropriate behavioral responses; reducing effects of cognitive impairment; special needs of persons with developmental and mental disorders including cerebral palsy, epilepsy, Parkinson's disease, and mental illness

Training Topic / Competency Item: CNA Annual In-Service Training: 24 hours of varied in-service training per year. Content must address: areas of weakness from performance reviews; special needs of patients with cognitive needs; deficiencies cited in last licensing survey. Includes 4 hours of resident abuse training every 2 years.
Purpose: Annual In-Service
Approval Basis: CDPH-approved in-service program
Notes / Research Flags: Facility must submit in-service schedule for CDPH approval. Topics must include multiple subjects. Shall address patient special needs and survey deficiency areas. 4-hr resident abuse training is a mandatory sub-requirement on a 2-year cycle. | Per §71847(f)(15), infection control is an explicitly enumerated in-service topic: universal precautions; handling patients and materials soiled with blood/body fluids; methods to reduce transmission of infectious agents.

Training Topic / Competency Item: Mandated Reporter / Elder and Dependent Adult Abuse Training: all staff who provide direct care must receive training on recognizing, detecting, and reporting elder and dependent adult abuse and neglect under CANRA (Penal Code §11164 et seq.) and EADACPA (WIC §15630 et seq.)
Purpose: Initial + Periodic
Approval Basis: facility-administered
Notes / Research Flags: Mandatory reporter obligations apply to SNF staff. Training content must cover recognition of abuse/neglect/exploitation, mandatory reporting obligations, and documentation requirements.

Training Topic / Competency Item: Nurse Assistant New Employee Orientation: 16 hours total - first 8 hours before direct patient care (at facility where employed); remaining 8 hours within the next 32 hours of employment. First 8-hour content: (1) facility tour, patient population overview, equipment use including call cord/intercommunication; (2) emergency and disaster preparedness; (3) supervised basic patient care clinical training. Second 8-hour content: role of nurse assistant, job description, team approach; personnel policies; patient care policies and procedures including ADLs, transfers, positioning.
Purpose: Initial (New Hire Orientation)
Approval Basis: CDPH-approved orientation program required; clinical training must be conducted by Director of Staff Development or licensed nurse free of other responsibilities
Frequency: One-time (new hire, prior to direct patient care)
Notes / Research Flags: Distinct from NATP initial certification program (§71835) - applies to already-certified CNAs joining a new facility and to non-certified nurse assistants prior to entering a certification program. Non-certified nurse assistants may only provide care in areas where orientation and demonstrated competency have been completed. ⚠️ SME FLAG: Confirm whether this orientation requirement applies exclusively to nurse assistants or has broader application to all new clinical staff under 22 CCR §72521.

Training Topic / Competency Item: Dementia-Specific Orientation Training (Dementia Training Standards Act of 2001): minimum 2 hours of dementia-specific training completed as part of the facility's orientation program, within the first 40 hours of employment.
Purpose: Initial (New Hire Orientation)
Approval Basis: facility-administered; incorporated into CDPH-approved orientation program
Notes / Research Flags: Per Dementia Training Standards Act of 2001 (HSC §1263). Exemption: freestanding and hospital-based pediatric SNFs with exclusively pediatric occupancy are exempt. Distinct from Module 12 of NATP (§71835(n)) which covers cognitive impairment for pre-certification trainees - this obligation applies to already-certified CNAs joining a new facility. Content must be dementia-specific.

Training Topic / Competency Item: Dementia-Specific Annual In-Service Training (Dementia Training Standards Act of 2001): minimum 5 hours of dementia-specific in-service training per year, incorporated as part of the facility's 24-hour annual CNA in-service program.
Purpose: Annual In-Service
Approval Basis: incorporated into CDPH-approved annual in-service program (22 CCR §71847)
Notes / Research Flags: Per Dementia Training Standards Act of 2001 (HSC §1263(c)). These 5 hours count toward (not in addition to) the 24-hr annual CNA in-service requirement under 22 CCR §71847 - CDPH tracks compliance with this sub-requirement independently. Pediatric SNF exemption applies. Separately enumerated from the 4-hr resident abuse training (HSC §1337.1(e)(2)) within the same in-service bundle. ⚠️ SME FLAG: Confirm whether 5 hours is counted within or additive to the 24-hr annual in-service requirement.

Oversight / Professional Agency: California Department of Public Health - Nursing Home Administrator Program (NHAP)
Training Topic / Competency Item: Nursing Home Administrator (NHA) Continuing Education: 40 hours of NHAP-approved continuing education required per 2-year license renewal period; minimum 10 of the 40 hours must be specifically in the area of aging or patient care. Approved CE subject areas: law and regulation; financial management; human resources; quality improvement and quality assurance; organizational management; patient care and aging.
Purpose: License Renewal CE
Approval Basis: NHAP-approved continuing education providers (CEPs) only; NCERS-approved CE also accepted
Notes / Research Flags: Administered by the Nursing Home Administrator Program (NHAP) within CDPH. Governed by Health and Safety Code §§1416–1416.84. CE certificates must be retained by licensee for 4 years. Inactive license holders exempt from CE during inactive period but must still renew. Distinct from federal NHA requirements under 42 CFR §483.70 (facility administrator competency requirements) and from CMS State Operations Manual guidance. Analog: RCFE Administrator CE under HSC §1569.616 applies in ALF setting.
